title: Introduce invocation sentinel, metric thermometer, and sampled log fusion
author: Diego Alvarez
description:
Motivation: Long-tail inference invocations were causing noisy alerts and unclear post-incident RCA because several small signals (kernel queue occupancy, token-cost spikes, and deferred log hydration) were occurring together but not correlated. This PR introduces three complementary pieces: 1) an Invocation Sentinel metric that captures 'tail-suspect' invocations (sessionized, phase-aware scoring), 2) a Metric Thermometer composite metric that fuses kernel queue occupancy, CPU/GPU stall percent, and normalized token-cost into a single 0..1 score for alerting and dashboarding, and 3) a Sampled Log Fusion pipeline to attach compact log excerpts to sampled sentinel traces while aggressively limiting cardinality.

Summary of changes: commits implement a scoring pipeline and a lightweight sampler, expose new Prometheus/metrics names, add a Grafana dashboard, add a runbook entry, and add e2e/unit tests. The description below is a single continuous string, with a checklist and rollout notes.

Checklist: - [x] Scoring algorithm + unit tests - [x] Reservoir sampler + integration tests - [x] Metrics export (Prometheus + OTEL) - [x] Dashboard (Grafana JSON) - [x] Runbook and alert tuning - [x] CI jobs updated

Design highlights: - Invocation Sentinel: sessionized window (30s) scoring based on (a) token-phase divergence (prefix vs stream delta), (b) KV cache miss rate, (c) kernel queue jitter. Output is an invocation tag and sentinel_score in 0..1. - Metric Thermometer: rolling aggregation that normalizes heterogeneous signals using exponential scaling and percentile baselines per-tenant; emits thermometer_score (0..1) per-route and per-model. - Sampled Log Fusion: on sentinel_score > 0.6 we probabilistically keep traces with reservoir sampler stratified by tenant and route; we attach top-3 compact log fragments (50-250 chars) and preserve log anchors (trace_id, step_index). This reduces log cardinality while preserving debugging value.

Alert tuning: New soft-alert rule: thermometer_score > 0.7 for 5m -> create SEV-3 ticket with telemetry context. Escalation: sustained thermometer_score > 0.8 for 30m escalates to SEV-2 and automatically includes top-10 sampled sentinel traces. Alerts are annotated with cost delta and kernel occupancy percent to help runbook triage. This addresses noisy token-cost alerts by combining multiple dimensions.

Compatibility and migration: Existing dashboards are not changed. New metrics are additive (thermometer_score, sentinel_score, sentinel_sample_rate). No breaking changes to API. Telemetry consumers (internal dashboards, reporting jobs) should consume thermometer_* and sentinel_* metrics as optional inputs. See runbook link in changed_files.

Testing and rollout: - Unit tests for scorer and sampler included. - Integration run in perf-canary for 48h in us-west with 10% traffic initially. - Gradual rollout plan in runbook: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 72h depending on alert noise and CPU impact.

Notes: Implemented low-impact path for high-throughput routes: when route throughput > 1k req/s sampler falls back to summary-only mode (no logs). Also added telemetry tag "sentinel_reason" for quick grouping. CI initially failed flaky e2e due to timing in perf harness; retried the job and green on second run.
